result.reason: Both items constitute the baraita establishing Rabbi Yishmael's position — item 1 opens the question and item 2 provides the analogical reasoning — which is precisely what the 'Rabbi Yishmael' section's prose describes.

Both items directly address the correction of the baraita regarding edim zomemim and the bo'el — item 1 raises the verse applied to the bo'el and item 2 corrects it — which is precisely what the 'Bo'el Punishment' prose describes: the Gemara's textual correction that zomemim receive chenek (the bo'el's punishment) rather than srefah.

All 7 items cover the Rabbi Yishmael vs. Rabbi Akiva dispute over 'bas u'vas,' the gezeirah shavah excluding the pnuya, and Rabbi Yishmael's possible misreading of Rabbi Akiva as abandoning the gezeirah shavah — exactly the content described in the 'Dibra Torah Principle' prose.

All seven items discuss exactly what candidate 0's prose covers: Rabbi Yishmael's use of the extra vav (u'vas) for the blemished bat kohen teaching, Rabbi Akiva's derivation from v'hayu kodesh, and the et aviha hi mechalelet exposition including Rabbi Meir's baraita and Rav Ashi's remark — all of which are explicitly described in the 'Vav as Exclusion' prose.

The passage describes Rabbi Yehuda's alternative method of forcing open the mouth with tongs to fulfill mitzvas srefah, which directly matches the 'Mouth Opening' section's prose about Rabbi Yehuda's objection and proposed solution using tzavas.
The passage is the exact Rabbi Elazar ben Tzadok testimony about the priest's daughter case that the 'Historical Case' prose explicitly describes and discusses.
The passage directly asks what kind of 'ptilah' (wick) the mishna refers to and gives Rav Mattana's answer of a lead wick, which is precisely what the 'Ptilah Identity' section's prose describes.

Both items present the two competing *gezeirah shavah* derivations (from Korach's congregation and from Nadav and Avihu) for the soul-burning method of *srefah*, which is precisely what Candidate 0's prose describes and labels 'Two Models'.

All three items discuss the derivation from the assembly of Korah regarding sreifas neshamah v'guf kayam, including the interpretation of 'b'nafshosam' and Reish Lakish's reading about flattery and eating — exactly what the 'Korach Analysis' prose section discusses.

All three items discuss the interpretation of the deaths of Nadav and Avihu (sons of Aaron) — specifically whether 'vayamutu' implies the body was intact, whether the fire was internal or external, and what 'vatokhal otam' means — which matches exactly the prose under heading 0 ('Nadav Avihu').

All four items form the continuous question-and-answer chain about deriving srefah from parim hanisrafim versus human models, which is precisely what the 'Human Models' prose section describes in detail.

All four items form a continuous Talmudic discussion about the mercy principle (ve'ahavta lerei'acha kamocha / beror lo misa yafa) and its relationship to the gezeirah shavah, which is precisely what the 'Mercy Principle' section's prose describes in detail.
The passage depicts Nadav and Avihu's ambitious conversation about outliving Moses and Aaron and God's response, which is precisely what the 'Ambition' section's prose describes.

The passage is Rabbi Eliezer's parable about a Torah scholar's diminishing status in an ignoramus's eyes, which the prose of 'Seduction Strategy' explicitly discusses and connects to Korach's strategy of hospitality undermining the leaders' critical detachment.
Both items together describe the Rav Chama bar Toviyya case (item 1) and Rav Yosef's verdict that he erred in two ways (item 2), which is precisely what the 'Rav Chama Case' prose discusses.

The passage directly quotes the mishna's incident with a priest's daughter and Rav Yosef's identification of the Sadducean court, which is precisely what the 'Testimony Dismissal' prose discusses in detail.

All three items form a single continuous Talmudic discussion about harmonizing the two accounts of Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok — establishing there were two incidents and working out their logical order — which is precisely what the 'Two Accounts' prose describes.
